title: Ramsagar Wildlife Sanctuary
tagline: Ramsagar Wildlife Sanctuary — Wetland Wilderness, Chambal Ravines & Historic Dholpur Heritage

heroImage.alt: Ramsagar Wildlife Sanctuary in Dholpur, Rajasthan, India

overview.short: Ramsagar Wildlife Sanctuary in Dholpur, Rajasthan, protects picturesque Ramsagar Lake, sheltering marsh crocodiles, migratory waterfowl, and the rich heritage of the Chambal valley.
overview.description: Located in Dholpur district on the border of Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, Ramsagar Wildlife Sanctuary centers around the picturesque Ramsagar Lake, an extensive artificial reservoir built in the late 19th century by the Maharajas of Dholpur. The sanctuary covers 34.4 square kilometers of pristine aquatic and scrubland ecosystems, providing critical breeding grounds for resident marsh crocodiles (muggers), freshwater softshell turtles, and thousands of winter migratory waterfowl including painted storks, pelicans, and ringed plovers. Nestled amid the rugged Vindhyan ravines, it offers easy access to historic Dholpur treasures like the 108-temple Machkund complex, the Mughal lakeside retreat of Talab-e-Shahi, and the renowned National Chambal Sanctuary.
overview.about: A hidden jewel of eastern Rajasthan, Ramsagar is an oasis for birdwatchers and heritage seekers. Visitors can combine boat safaris on the Chambal river, birdwatching across Ramsagar and Talab-e-Shahi lakes, and exploring centuries-old red sandstone palaces and medieval citadels.

howToReach.roadNote: Easily accessible via NH-44 (Delhi-Agra-Gwalior highway) and RJ SH-23 from Dholpur and Bari. Well connected to Agra (65 km), Gwalior (70 km), and Jaipur (210 km).

topPlaces.name: Ramsagar Lake & Wetland Reserve
topPlaces.description: Expansive historic reservoir created by Dholpur royals, renowned for picturesque sunset reflections, marsh crocodiles, and flocks of migratory ducks and pelicans.

image.alt: Ramsagar Lake & Wetland Reserve in Ramsagar Wildlife Sanctuary, Dholpur, Rajasthan

topPlaces.name: Machkund Sacred Tank & 108 Temple Complex
topPlaces.description: Revered ancient pilgrimage complex named after Suryavanshi King Muchkund, featuring 108 red sandstone temples built around a sacred stepped kund.

image.alt: Machkund Sacred Tank & 108 Temple Complex in Ramsagar Wildlife Sanctuary, Dholpur, Rajasthan

topPlaces.name: Talab-e-Shahi Lake & Mughal Palace (Bari)
topPlaces.description: Lakeside Mughal hunting pavilion and stepped masonry embankment constructed in 1617 by Prince Khurram (Emperor Shah Jahan) for royal sojourns.

image.alt: Talab-e-Shahi Lake & Mughal Palace (Bari) in Ramsagar Wildlife Sanctuary, Dholpur, Rajasthan

topPlaces.name: Van Vihar Wildlife Sanctuary (Dholpur Plateau)
topPlaces.description: Sprawling 60-sq-km reserve along the Vindhyan plateau preserving dry deciduous dhok forests, chital, blue bulls, leopards, and sambar deer.

image.alt: Van Vihar Wildlife Sanctuary (Dholpur Plateau) in Ramsagar Wildlife Sanctuary, Dholpur, Rajasthan

topPlaces.name: National Chambal Sanctuary (Gharial Safari Ghat)
topPlaces.description: Crystal-clear Chambal river sanctuary offering boat safaris to observe critically endangered gharials, Gangetic dolphins, marsh muggers, and Indian skimmers.

image.alt: National Chambal Sanctuary (Gharial Safari Ghat) in Ramsagar Wildlife Sanctuary, Dholpur, Rajasthan

topPlaces.name: Shergarh Fort (Chambal Riverfront Citadel)
topPlaces.description: Formidable 800-year-old stone fort perched high above the Chambal River, fortified by Sher Shah Suri in 1540 with commanding ravine watchtowers.

image.alt: Shergarh Fort (Chambal Riverfront Citadel) in Ramsagar Wildlife Sanctuary, Dholpur, Rajasthan

topPlaces.name: Royal Dholpur Bawdi (Historic Stepped Reservoir)
topPlaces.description: Ancient royal red sandstone stepwell showcasing intricate multi-tiered masonry steps, arched water chambers, and traditional rainwater conservation engineering.

image.alt: Royal Dholpur Bawdi historic stepwell in Dholpur, Rajasthan

topPlaces.name: Raj Niwas Palace & Dholpur Heritage Enclave
topPlaces.description: Magnificent 19th-century royal palace built from Dholpur’s world-famous red and beige sandstone, adorned with Belgian chandeliers and Mughal garden pavilions.

image.alt: Raj Niwas Palace & Dholpur Heritage Enclave in Ramsagar Wildlife Sanctuary, Dholpur, Rajasthan

itinerary.title: Day 1 — Ramsagar Lake Birding, Talab-e-Shahi & Machkund

items.note: Start early around Ramsagar reservoir for winter waterfowl and marsh muggers.
Explore the 1617 Shah Jahan hunting pavilion and serene lakeside walkways in Bari.
Walk through red sandstone pavilions and sacred bathing ghats bathed in afternoon sunlight.
View the illuminated 8-storey clock tower and try local Dholpuri pedas and street snacks.

itinerary.title: Day 2 — National Chambal River Safari & Shergarh Fort

items.note: Take an authorized motorized boat safari to see basking gharials, softshell turtles, and skimmers.
Explore medieval bastion gates and panoramic views overlooking the Chambal ravines.

faq.q: What is the best season to visit Ramsagar Wildlife Sanctuary?
faq.a: October to March is the best time, when temperatures are pleasant (8°C to 24°C) and thousands of migratory birds arrive at Ramsagar and Talab-e-Shahi lakes.

faq.q: What wildlife species can be seen in Ramsagar Sanctuary?
faq.a: Ramsagar supports marsh crocodiles (muggers), freshwater turtles, painted storks, pelicans, wild boars, hyenas, and jackals.

faq.q: Can Ramsagar be visited alongside the Chambal Safari?
faq.a: Yes, Ramsagar is just 35 km from the Chambal river safari ghats, making it ideal for a combined 2-day wildlife and heritage itinerary.
